_note: Public guidance underpinning the preparedness checklists of Disaster Compass Central Asia. key is referenced by site checklists; audience: company|individual|both; confirmed_by records how each statement was verified in this research session (page_read = fetched and read; third_party = secondary source fetched; search_snippet = WebSearch result summary only; unverified = from memory). CHECKPOINT - being refined.

items.recommendation_ja: Plan relief water at Sphere minimums: 2.5-3 L per person per day for drinking plus 2-6 L for hygiene and 3-6 L for cooking, i.e. 7.5-15 L per person per day in total (15 L is the usual planning figure).
items.source_name: Sphere Handbook 2018, WASH water supply standard 2.1

items.recommendation_ja: Store at least 1 gallon (about 3.8 L) of water per person per day for drinking and sanitation, for a minimum of 3 days and ideally 2 weeks, with the same duration of non-perishable food.
items.quantitative: 1 gal (3.8 L)/person/day; min 3 days, better 2 weeks
items.source_name: Ready.gov (FEMA) - Water / Build a Kit

items.recommendation_ja: When shaking starts: Drop, Cover and Hold On until it stops. Beforehand, secure heavy furniture, shelves, water heaters and TVs to walls so they cannot fall on people or block exits.
items.source_name: Ready.gov (FEMA) - Earthquakes

items.recommendation_ja: Expect aftershocks: most large earthquakes are followed by smaller quakes that can still damage weakened buildings, with the rate decreasing over days to months. Do not re-enter damaged buildings and keep exits clear.
items.quantitative: USGS forecasts aftershocks over 1 day, 1 week, 1 month and 1 year
items.source_name: USGS Aftershock Forecast Overview

items.recommendation_ja: Turn Around, Don't Drown: never walk or drive into flood water. About 15 cm (6 in) of moving water can knock an adult down and about 30 cm (1 ft) can float a car.
items.quantitative: 15 cm knocks down an adult; 30 cm floats a car
items.source_name: NWS / FEMA - Turn Around Don't Drown

items.recommendation_ja: Adopt a heat-health action plan: act on heat warnings, shift outdoor work to cooler hours, provide water and cool rooms, and check on elderly, chronically ill and outdoor workers daily during heat waves.
items.source_name: WHO - Heat and health

items.recommendation_ja: During cold waves keep indoor temperatures adequate, layer clothing and watch for hypothermia and frostbite. Never run generators, charcoal or gas heaters indoors or in garages: carbon monoxide poisoning kills quickly.
items.source_name: WHO - Cold weather and health

items.recommendation_ja: If tap water may be contaminated, bring it to a rolling boil for 1 minute (3 minutes above about 2,000 m) or use bottled water; if boiling is impossible, use household chlorine and wait 30 minutes.
items.quantitative: Boil 1 min (3 min at high altitude)
items.source_name: CDC - Making Water Safe in an Emergency

items.recommendation_ja: Avoid wading in flood water with bare feet or open cuts; wear waterproof boots and gloves and cover wounds. Fever, headache and muscle pain 2-30 days after contact need medical review for leptospirosis.
items.source_name: CDC - Leptospirosis

items.recommendation_ja: Agree a written family plan: two meeting points (near home and outside the neighborhood), an out-of-area contact everyone reports to, and how to reach children's schools; practice it twice a year.
items.source_name: IFRC / Red Cross Red Crescent - family emergency plan

items.recommendation_ja: Run business continuity as a management system per ISO 22301:2019: business impact analysis and risk assessment, continuity strategies, documented response plans, exercises at planned intervals, and management review.
items.source_name: ISO 22301:2019 Security and resilience - BCMS - Requirements

items.recommendation_ja: Small and medium enterprises should keep a simple BCP: identify critical functions and suppliers, set recovery time objectives, back up data off-site, and rehearse the plan with staff.
items.source_name: UNDRR / PreventionWeb - business continuity for SMEs

items.recommendation_ja: Keep emergency alerts (cell broadcast) switched on in phone settings so government warnings reach the handset within seconds without a subscription; Kazakhstan's MES is rolling out such a Mass Alert system alongside 112 SMS.
items.source_name: Wikipedia - Cell Broadcast (public warning implementations)

items.recommendation_ja: In Kazakhstan dial 112 for all emergencies (101 fire, 102 police, 103 ambulance also work); warnings arrive as SMS from '112' and, in Almaty and other regions, as Mass Alert cell-broadcast messages. Verify the MES app before relying on it.
items.source_name: Kazakhstan MES (via libphonenumber short-number data and press reports)

items.recommendation_ja: Register with your embassy so it can reach you in a crisis: Japanese nationals file the Overseas Residential Registration (ORRnet) for stays of 3 months or more or Tabireg for shorter trips; US citizens enrol in STEP; UK nationals subscribe to FCDO travel-advice email alerts.
items.source_name: MOFA Japan ORRnet / US State Dept STEP / UK FCDO

items.recommendation_ja: Make sure every registered family member receives the embassy's emergency e-mails (Japan: consular e-mails sent to ORRnet/Tabireg registrants) and store the embassy's emergency phone number in each phone.
items.source_name: MOFA Japan - Overseas Safety

items.recommendation_ja: Give every family member a wallet card with emergency numbers, the out-of-area contact, meeting points, school and workplace numbers and medical notes, and keep a copy in each child's bag.
items.source_name: Ready.gov (FEMA) - Make a Plan / family communication card

items.recommendation_ja: Keep a reserve of prescription medicines for chronic conditions (7-14 days) together with a list of generic drug names and doses, and rotate it before expiry.
items.source_name: CDC / Ready.gov - emergency supply of medicines

items.recommendation_ja: Include pets in the plan: carrier, leash, 2 weeks of food and water, vaccination records and photos, and identify pet-friendly shelters or boarding in advance since public shelters may refuse animals.
items.quantitative: 2 weeks of pet food and water
items.source_name: Ready.gov (FEMA) - Pets and Animals

items.recommendation_ja: In the Almaty foothills avoid river valleys and gorges during and after heavy rain or rapid snowmelt (mudflow season May-September), heed Kazselezashchita/MES sirens and SMS, and move sideways uphill away from the channel.
items.source_name: Kazselezashchita / Kazhydromet mudflow hazard bulletins

items.recommendation_ja: In winter follow CoES avalanche warnings: avoid unnecessary travel on mountain roads (Dushanbe-Khujand, Dushanbe-Khorog, Khorog-Ishkashim), keep extra distance between vehicles, and carry warm clothing, food and a charged phone when driving passes.
items.source_name: Tajikistan Committee of Emergency Situations and Civil Defence (CoES) warnings via Asia-Plus

items.recommendation_ja: On smoky or heavily polluted days (PM2.5 above the WHO 24-hour guideline of 15 µg/m3 by several times) limit outdoor exertion, keep windows closed and use a well-fitted N95/FFP2 respirator outdoors; cloth and surgical masks do not filter fine particles.
items.quantitative: WHO AQG 2021: PM2.5 15 µg/m3 (24 h), 5 µg/m3 (annual)
items.source_name: WHO global air quality guidelines 2021 / CDC respirator advice

items.recommendation_ja: Hold evacuation and shelter drills at least once a year (more often where local fire rules require), and include expatriate families and new hires in at least one drill.
items.source_name: ISO 22301 exercising requirement / local fire-safety rules

items.recommendation_ja: If flood water is rising and roads are already cut, move to the highest floor of a solid building (vertical evacuation) rather than driving; avoid closed attics without an exit and switch off electricity before water reaches outlets.
items.source_name: Ready.gov (FEMA) - Floods

items.recommendation_ja: Prepare for winter outages: a safe backup heat source and fuel, insulation for one room, warm layers and blankets, and a battery or generator kept outdoors away from windows with a CO alarm indoors.
items.quantitative: Generator at least 6 m (20 ft) from windows
items.source_name: Ready.gov (FEMA) - Winter Weather / CDC

items.recommendation_ja: Operate a safety-confirmation (roll-call) system that pushes a 'are you safe?' message over several channels and collects replies for all staff, expatriate families and travellers; test it twice a year and track response rate and time.
items.source_name: ISO 22301 warning and communication requirements

items.recommendation_ja: Keep at least one communication path that does not depend on local mobile networks (satellite phone or satellite messenger) at each site, check local licensing rules, and test it monthly.
items.source_name: UN Emergency Telecommunications Cluster / FEMA Ready Business
